unit.title: C2 Mastery — The Capstone
unit.subtitle: A triumphant review of the whole A1→C2 journey

grammar.title: You've reached the summit
grammar.intro: This is the final unit of the entire course. From hola to the literary -ra, you've climbed all six CEFR levels. This capstone weaves together the C2 threads — main-clause subjunctive, the values of se, queísmo/dequeísmo, expressive morphology, pragmatics, rhetoric, refranes and the mot juste. Review them once more, then celebrate: you now command Spanish at a near-native level. ¡Enhorabuena!

sections.heading: Main-clause subjunctive & the literary -ra
sections.body: The subjunctive escapes subordinate clauses: wishes with ojalá / quién + imperfect subjunctive (¡Quién pudiera!), blessings (Que te vaya bien), and the literary -ra standing in for the pluperfect indicative (el discurso que pronunciara = había pronunciado).
conj: may it go well for you

ex.en: If only one could master so many nuances!

ex.es: La novela que escribiera en su juventud sigue viva.
ex.en: The novel he had written in his youth is still alive.

sections.heading: The values of se & de vs que
sections.body: Se covers reflexive, reciprocal, impersonal (se dice), passive refleja (se venden pisos) and the involuntary (se me cayó). Meanwhile, watch the preposition: dequeísmo adds a wrong de (pienso de que ✗), queísmo drops a needed one (me acuerdo que ✗ → de que).

ex.es: Se me cayeron las llaves sin querer.

sections.heading: Diminutives, augmentatives & discourse markers
sections.body: Expressive suffixes carry attitude: -ito softens (un momentito), -azo augments or hits (un golazo), -ucho disparages (un cuartucho). Pragmatic markers frame tone: a decir verdad, la verdad sea dicha, dicho sea de paso, ahora bien.

ex.es: A decir verdad, el plan no me convence del todo.
ex.en: To tell the truth, the plan doesn't entirely convince me.
He lived in a wretched little room with no windows.

sections.heading: Refranes, Latinisms, irony & the mot juste
sections.body: The finishing touches: refranes (más vale tarde que nunca), Latinisms used correctly (grosso modo, motu proprio, statu quo — no stray a- or de-), irony and connotation, correlatives (no solo… sino) and native collocations (surtir efecto, zanjar). This is the register that reads as truly educated Spanish.

ex.es: Lo explicó grosso modo, sin entrar en detalles.
ex.en: He explained it roughly, without going into detail.

ex.es: Vino motu proprio, sin que nadie se lo pidiera.
ex.en: He came of his own accord, without anyone asking him.

takeaways: The subjunctive lives in main clauses too: ¡Quién pudiera!, Que te vaya bien, and the literary -ra.
Master se (se me cayó, se venden) and avoid dequeísmo/queísmo (pienso que · me acuerdo de que).
Suffixes and discourse markers encode attitude; refranes and Latinisms polish the register.
You've completed A1→C2 — you now wield Spanish with near-native precision. ¡Enhorabuena!

mistakes.why: Pensar takes que with no de — adding it is dequeísmo.
The Latinism is grosso modo, with no preposition a.
The involuntary event needs the se construction: se me cayeron.

exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! estar seguro DE que — sin caer en queísmo.
exercises.no: It's “estar seguro de que”; dropping the de would be queísmo.

exercises.prompt: Ya te vas… Pues nada, que te ___ bien.
exercises.prompt_en: You're off already… Well then, may it go well for you.
exercises.no: The blessing “que te vaya bien” uses the main-clause subjunctive: vaya.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! se de involuntariedad → se me cayeron.
exercises.no: “Se me cayeron las llaves” — the involuntary se, with the verb agreeing with llaves (cayeron).

exercises.prompt: Lo explicó ___ modo, sin entrar en detalles.
exercises.prompt_en: He explained it roughly, without going into detail.
exercises.no: The Latinism is “grosso modo” (never 'a grosso modo').

exercises.prompt: Match each Latin phrase to its meaning.

exercises.tts: A decir verdad, no me convence del todo.
accepted: a decir verdad no me convence del todo
exercises.translation: To tell the truth, it doesn't entirely convince me.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “A decir verdad, no me convence del todo.”
exercises.no: It was: “A decir verdad, no me convence del todo.” (a discourse marker framing tone).

exercises.scenario: A friend arrives late yet again ⏰

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.es: Ya sé, llego tarde otra vez… lo siento.
lines.en: I know, I'm late again… sorry.

options.text: Tranquila, más vale tarde que nunca.
Tranquila, vale más nunca que tarde.
Tranquila, más vale tarde que jamás nunca.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! El refrán es “más vale tarde que nunca”.
exercises.no: The set proverb is “más vale tarde que nunca” — the other two garble it.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Un cierre digno de un C2. ¡Enhorabuena!
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Ojalá nunca deje de aprender.”

vocab.en: may it go well for you
